# SYMBOLS.md — C ⇄ Rust dynamic-symbol parity

Generated by `./gen_symbols.sh` from `nm -D --defined-only` on the built shared
objects.  Not hand-maintained.

## What the C build produces

For one `(HASH_BACKEND, THASH, SECPAR)` configuration CMake emits three shared
objects (plus the `driver` executable):

| C shared object | sources | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `app/libsphincs_core.so` | `address.c fors.c merkle.c sign.c utils.c utilsx1.c wots.c wotsx1.c` + `randombytes.c` | `randombytes` reads `/dev/urandom`; `void` return |
| `app/libsphincs_core_det.so` | the same object files + `rng.c` | `randombytes` is the NIST AES-256-CTR-DRBG; `int` return |
| `lib/<be>/lib<be>.so` | the backend's `<be>.c hash_<be>.c thash_<be>_<THASH>.c` (+ `utils.c` for sha2/blake) | provides `SPX_thash`, `SPX_prf_addr`, … |

The Rust crate is a single `cdylib` (`libsphincs_plus.so`) that has to cover the
union of all three.  The Rust `randombytes` is the `rng.c` (DRBG) one — the
`randombytes.c` `/dev/urandom` variant is translated as
`randombytes_urandom` with no `#[no_mangle]`, because the two cannot share the
linker name `randombytes` inside one object.  That matches the `driver`, which
CMake links against `sphincs_core_det`.

## Per-configuration symbol tables

`nm` type letters: `T` = text (function), `R` = read-only data,
`B` = uninitialised data.  "Rust" is ✅ when the Rust `cdylib` for the matching
feature combination exports the same name.

## Rust-side undefined symbols

`nm -D --undefined-only` on the Rust `cdylib` lists only glibc / libgcc-unwind
imports (`memcpy`, `malloc`, `_Unwind_*`, …) — there is no unresolved
project-level symbol:
